answer: A practical defence is requiring each agent to post a refundable stake plus proof of useful work before it can trade. The stake is slashed if peers catch fraud, and the work must be unique, so copying one identity does not create a second valid one. Like a wharf that only unloads cargo after inspection, an attacker can repaint many fake hulls with fresh pigment, but each hull still needs its own paid berth and inspected cargo. An opal can be copied in appearance, but not its deposit and verified history, so thousands of fakes cost thousands of stakes, while honest agents pay only once.
